title: FDA takes on GLP-1 compounding boom with warnings about misleading marketing
summary: The FDA issued more than 50 warning letters to telehealth companies, concierge practices, and medical spas selling compounded semaglutide/tirzepatide, focused on false claims that the compounded drugs are equivalent to FDA-approved medicines.

title: Telehealth Booms as Demand for GLP-1s Surges and Questions Mount About Safety, Oversight
summary: Investigation into the grey-market/telehealth GLP-1 boom: medication-error reports involving GLP-1s rose from ~2,000 (2020) to more than 25,000 (2025), and poison-control overdose calls jumped nearly 1,500% since 2019, with several patient-harm case studies from compounded prescriptions.

title: Lilly sues online vendors, medical spa over copycat weight-loss drugs
summary: Eli Lilly filed a fresh round of lawsuits against online vendors and a medical spa selling compounded 'copycat' tirzepatide, alleging false advertising. By this point Lilly had already sued more than two dozen med spas, wellness centers and compounders.

title: ITC issues General Exclusion Order on tirzepatide and knock-off 'tirzepatide' products
publisher: U.S. International Trade Commission / Federal Register
summary: The ITC issued a General Exclusion Order directing U.S. Customs to block imports of knock-off tirzepatide products, after finding seven entities likely to deceive consumers about whether their imported 'tirzepatide' was genuine, FDA-approved, or contained the drug at all. Stemmed from an Eli Lilly complaint.

title: FDA clarifies compounding policy as GLP-1 shortages resolve, setting enforcement deadlines
summary: FDA declared the tirzepatide shortage resolved (Dec 19, 2024) and the semaglutide shortage resolved (Feb 21, 2025), ending the enforcement-discretion window that had let compounders mass-produce the drugs. This is the regulatory event that legally ended the compounded-GLP-1 boom.

title: United States v. Matthew Kawa et al. — Paradigm Peptides guilty plea
publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, USAO Northern District of Indiana
summary: Matthew Kawa and Jennifer Stechkober pleaded guilty over the operation of Paradigm Peptides, which sold SARMs, hCG and peptides nationwide; federal investigators found products labeled as SARMs actually contained testosterone (a Schedule III controlled substance) and that the peptide/hCG products were unapproved new drugs. Kawa also owned Amino Asylum.

title: Eli Lilly names Paradigm Peptides as a respondent in ITC tirzepatide complaint
summary: Eli Lilly's ITC complaint over imported knock-off tirzepatide named Paradigm Peptides of Michigan City, Indiana among the respondents, part of the investigation that led to the April 2025 General Exclusion Order.

title: FDA Warning Letter to SwissChems (MARCS-CMS 695663)
summary: FDA cited SwissChems for marketing semaglutide and retatrutide as unapproved new drugs intended for human use, using the company's own product-page language as evidence. Issued the same day as letters to Summit Research Peptides, Prime Peptides and Xcel Peptides in a coordinated peptide/GLP-1 warning-letter wave.

title: Amino Asylum's Memphis warehouse raided by federal agents; site goes dark
summary: Multiple industry sources report federal agents raided Amino Asylum's Memphis, TN warehouse around June 18, 2025, with the website going offline. Reported by forum/affiliate sources, not mainstream press, but the underlying conduct was later confirmed by owner Matthew Kawa's Dec 2025 DOJ guilty plea. Date is approximate.

title: Peptide Sciences shuts down — largest U.S. grey-market peptide vendor exits
summary: Peptide Sciences, described by industry trackers as the largest U.S. grey-market peptide vendor, announced a voluntary shutdown. Reported by industry retrospectives rather than mainstream news; exact date and framing are as claimed by those trackers and unverified independently.

title: Science.bio announces voluntary closure
summary: Research-chemical vendor Science.bio announced a voluntary wind-down, committing to refunds or order fulfillment; commentators framed it as a signal of a broader retreat from the grey market amid enforcement pressure. Reported by industry blogs/trackers, not mainstream news.

title: The FDA's War on Peptides: A 2024–2026 Enforcement Timeline
summary: Industry-analysis timeline compiling the 2023 FDA reclassification of ~17 peptides (BPC-157, TB-500, CJC-1295, etc.), the Dec 2024 warning-letter wave, and the 2025 GLP-1 shortage resolutions. An industry site (affiliate-adjacent), not independent journalism; publication date approximate.
